Subject: Annual prepay cadence and VAT handling questions

Hi Alex,

We are finalizing our annual prepay for 2027 and want to finalize the invoice cadence and withdrawal mechanics. A few concrete asks so we can onboard accounting: 

- Can you confirm the invoice cadence you recommend for a $250k annual commitment (monthly invoices vs. quarterly)?
- We need a sample invoice that shows line items, VAT where applicable, and payment instructions to push through our AP system.
- For BrightLabs EU entities: what VAT evidence do you need from us and what will Redwood include on the invoice (VAT number, reverse-charge note, etc.)?

If helpful, Accounting Ops has a PO template we can attach once cadence and VAT are agreed. We’re targeting first invoice on Jan 3, 2027 so payments are processed before the new quarter.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Finance | BrightLabs
jordan.price@brightlabs.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>

Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annual prepay cadence and VAT handling questions

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. High level recommendations for a $250k commitment: monthly invoices with a rolling withdrawal ladder (gives you regular granularity in AP and keeps burn visible). We typically issue an invoice on the 1st of each month for the prior month’s consumption allocated against the prepay, with a short statement showing remaining prepay balance.

Quick answers:
- Recommended cadence: monthly invoices (we can do quarterly if your AP prefers bulk processing).
- Sample invoice: attached below by Kimberly (PDF) — it includes VAT line, Redwood VAT number, and a reverse-charge note for EU customers where applicable.
- VAT evidence: we require the customer VAT number + entity name and, for some jurisdictions, a W-8 / local tax residency certificate. Kimberly will attach the standard VAT certificate we request. If PwC or your tax team wants to review wording we can loop them.

Next steps: 
1) Kimberly to drop the sample invoice and VAT certificate.
2) Priyom will share the withdrawal ladder (monthly drawdown schedule + holdback logic).
3) If BrightLabs can confirm preferred billing day (1st vs 3rd) and provide PO number, we’ll lock the January invoice.

Onward —
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai

Jordan / Alex —

Sharing the proposed withdrawal ladder and mechanics. Key points included in the spreadsheet (attached):

- prepay_withdrawal_ladder_v1.xlsx: a month-by-month drawdown table that debits consumption against the committed spend. Columns: month, starting balance, monthly consumption estimate, invoiced amount, remaining balance, holdback (10% reserved for last quarter adjustments).
- Invoice timing: we’ll issue an invoice on the billing day you confirm (default: 1st). Invoices will reflect net fees + VAT where applicable; if reverse-charge applies we leave VAT at 0% and include the reverse-charge note.
- Holdback & reconciliation: a 10% holdback is recommended to cover usage delta at year-end. The year-end reconciliation will produce a final true-up invoice/credit.

I’ve annotated the sheet with a suggested schedule for Jan–Dec 2027 and left a column for BrightLabs AP to populate expected monthly spend so you can see how the balance evolves.

Attachment stub: prepay_withdrawal_ladder_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

If this looks good I’ll circulate a PDF-friendly summary for your finance team.

— Priyom
